chunks: My shaykh Abu 'Abd Allah informed me, from Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Qulawayh, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, from Ahmad ibn Hilal, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from 'Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

There is no problem in performing wudu (ablution) with used water. And he said: the water with which a garment is washed, or with which a man performs ghusl from janabah, it is not permissible that wudu be performed from it, and similar things to it. But as for the water with which a man performs wudu, so he washes his face and his hand in a clean vessel, then there is no problem for another person to take it and perform wudu with it.

key_terms.الْجَنَابَةِ: the state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl
key_terms.الْمَاءِ الْمُسْتَعْمَلِ: used water that has already been employed for a prior washing act
key_terms.شَيْءٍ نَظِيفٍ: a clean container or clean receptacle
key_terms.غَيْرُهُ: another person besides the first user

ai.seo_question: Can wudu (ablution) be performed with used water in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a legal ruling on used water and its suitability for wudu (ablution). It distinguishes between water used for washing clothes or for ghusl from janabah, which is not to be used for wudu, and water used in wudu itself, which may be reused by another person when collected in a clean container.
